title: Mittag–Leffler cohomology for constant reductions on a weakly contractible affine
statement: Let $W$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] that is weakly contractible for its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], meaning that evaluation at the final object takes every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $J\subseteq A$ an ideal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived tensor [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $H\in D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},\underline A)$ be locally derived $J\underline A$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. Put $H_n=H\otimes_A^L\underline{A/J^n}$ with their canonical quotient transitions. Assume that for every $n\geq1$ there is $E_n\in D(A/J^n)$ and an isomorphism $H_n\simeq\underline{E_n}$, and that $E_1$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Then for every integer $q$ the inverse sequence of hypercohomology groups $H^q(W,H_n)$ is Mittag–Leffler: for each $n$ there is $m\geq n$ such that the images of $H^q(W,H_k)\to H^q(W,H_n)$ are equal for all $k\geq m$. Here hypercohomology is the cohomology of derived sections, as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The isomorphisms $H_n\simeq\underline{E_n}$ are not assumed compatible with the transition maps. No quotient $A/J^n$ is assumed finite as a set.

source.place: Tag 09C5, lemma-weakly-contractible-locally-constant-ML; all degrees follow by shifting. Its D_cons hypothesis is supplied here by complete H and constant perfect residue E_1. The proof uses Noetherian Artin–Rees, not finite underlying sets.

proof.text: If $W$ is empty, evaluation of every module sheaf at $W$ is zero (the empty covering gives a terminal section group), so the conclusion holds. Assume $W$ nonempty, and put $A_n=A/J^n$. Fix the given constant markings $H_n\simeq\underline{E_n}$. We will use the following elementary detection observation on every nonempty pro-étale object $U$: if a constant module sheaf $\underline T|_U$ is zero, then $T=0$. Indeed, the module sheafification of the constant presheaf has as underlying abelian sheaf the abelian sheafification [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], whose underlying sheaf of sets is the set sheafification [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets]. So if $t\in T$ has image $0$ in $\underline T(U)$, the sections $t$ and $0$ of the constant presheaf become equal after sheafification, hence agree on the members of some covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], i.e. $t=0$ in $T$ as soon as the covering has a member; pro-étale coverings are jointly surjective, so a covering of nonempty $U$ is a nonempty family. Constant realization is exact by the constant-module section lemma, so $H^i(\underline C)=\underline{H^i(C)}$. Applying the observation to the cohomology of a cone shows that constant realization on a nonempty $U$ reflects whether an algebraic derived morphism is an isomorphism. Constant realization also commutes with derived tensor: apply derived tensor pullback to the morphism from the sheaf topos to the one-point topos, with the constant coefficient ring. These identifications are natural in complexes and quotient maps. Here and below the canonical normalization of successive reductions is justified explicitly: choose a K-flat resolution with flat terms, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its scalar extension remains K-flat with flat terms by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. For ring maps $R\to S\to T$, the chain isomorphism $(K^\bullet\otimes_R S)\otimes_S T\to K^\bullet\otimes_R T$, $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes st$, with inverse $x\otimes t\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes t$, therefore computes derived successive extension. It commutes with every quotient unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. All rings used in the constant-exactness assertion, namely $A_n$ and later $B$, are Noetherian: for $A_n$ this follows because its ideals correspond to ideals of $A$ containing $J^n$.

source.place: Tag 09C5, preparatory constant-realization argument; sites-modules.tex Tags 093J–093K and sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4

proof.text: Every $E_n$ is perfect. To prove this without assuming compatible markings, put $F_n=E_n\otimes_{A_n}^L A_1$. Tensor associativity gives an isomorphism $\underline{F_n}\simeq H_n\otimes_{\underline{A_n}}^L\underline{A_1}\simeq H_1\simeq\underline{E_1}$. Apply the local-algebraicity lemma to its inverse $\underline{E_1}\to\underline{F_n}$ over $A_1$; its source is perfect by hypothesis. Choose a nonempty member of the resulting covering of $W$. There the inverse is the constant realization of a map $E_1\to F_n$. Step 1 reflects its being an isomorphism, so $F_n$ is perfect. The ideal $J/J^n$ in $A_n$ is nilpotent. Choose a bounded finite-projective representative $Q^\bullet$ of $F_n$, and apply nilpotent projective-complex lifting to $E_n$. It gives a bounded-above projective complex $P_n^\bullet$ with $P_n^\bullet/(J/J^n)P_n^\bullet\cong Q^\bullet$. If $Q^i=0$, then $P_n^i=(J/J^n)P_n^i$, and iterating the nilpotent ideal makes $P_n^i=0$. In the other finitely many degrees lift finite generators of $Q^i$ to $P_n^i$. The cokernel of the resulting finite free map equals its product with $J/J^n$, so is zero by the same iteration. Thus every term is finitely generated projective and $P_n^\bullet$ is bounded. This is exactly perfectness of $E_n$.

source.place: Tag 09C5, first paragraph; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 09BE; more-algebra.tex Tags 09AR and 07LU (explicit nilpotent Nakayama argument)

proof.text: Conjugate $H_{n+1}\to H_n$ by the chosen markings, obtaining $\underline{E_{n+1}}\to\underline{E_n}$ over $A_{n+1}$. Its source is perfect by step 2, so the local-algebraicity lemma supplies a covering on which it comes from an algebraic map $u_n:E_{n+1}\to E_n$ in $D(A_{n+1})$. Choose a nonempty member and one such $u_n$. Derived reduction gives a map $E_{n+1}\otimes_{A_{n+1}}^L A_n\to E_n$. Its constant realization on that member is the canonical normalization $H_{n+1}\otimes_{\underline{A_{n+1}}}^L\underline{A_n}\simeq H_n$, conjugated by the reduced markings. It is an isomorphism by tensor associativity, so step 1 detects that the algebraic reduction of $u_n$ is an isomorphism. Choose one $u_n$ for each $n$. Their composites make an algebraic tower with normalized reductions. We assert no global agreement between $\underline{u_n}$ and the original transitions.

source.place: Tag 09C5, first paragraph: choosing maps by Tag 09BE and checking their derived reductions

proof.text: Put $B=\widehat A=\varprojlim_nA/J^n$ and $I=JB$. Since $A$ is Noetherian, $J$ and all its powers are finitely generated. The completion-mod-ideal lemma makes $B$ $I$-adically complete. For each $n$, apply that lemma also to $J^n$: its completion is canonically $B$, since taking the subsequence of levels divisible by $n$ has inverse given at level $r$ by projecting from any level divisible by $n$ and at least $r$. These mutually inverse sequence maps commute with the projections to $A/J^n$. Since $(JB)^n=J^nB$, this gives $B/I^n\simeq A_n$ compatibly for every $n$. The completion-Noetherian lemma makes $B$ Noetherian. Apply perfect inverse-limit reconstruction over $B$ to the tower $(E_n,u_n)$ of step 3. Its residue $E_1$ is perfect and its normalized reductions are exactly those just constructed. Obtain a perfect $P\in D(B)$ and compatible isomorphisms $P\otimes_B^L B/I^n\simeq E_n$. Choose a bounded finite-projective representative $P^\bullet$. Its terms are flat (they are retracts of finite free modules), so its bounded tensor complex computes derived reduction; consequently we have individual isomorphisms $H_n\simeq\underline{P^\bullet/I^nP^\bullet}$.

source.place: Tag 09C5, algebraic reconstruction via more-algebra.tex Tag 09AW; algebra.tex Tags 05GG and 0316

proof.text: Fix an integer $q$ and write $Z^q=\ker(d^q:P^q\to P^{q+1})$ and $D^{q+1}=\operatorname{im}d^q$. Apply Artin–Rees over the Noetherian ring $B$ to $D^{q+1}\subseteq P^{q+1}$; the ambient module is finitely generated. Choose $c\geq0$ such that $D^{q+1}\cap I^tP^{q+1}\subseteq I^{t-c}D^{q+1}$ for $t\geq c$. For a fixed $n\geq1$ and $t\geq n+c$, a cycle modulo $I^t$ is represented by $z\in P^q$ with $dz\in I^tP^{q+1}$. Artin–Rees writes $dz$ as a finite sum $\sum a_jd(v_j)$ with $a_j\in I^{t-c}$; put $y=\sum a_jv_j\in I^{t-c}P^q\subseteq I^nP^q$. Then $z-y\in Z^q$ and has the same class as $z$ modulo $I^n$. Conversely any true cycle reduces to a cycle at every level. Thus, for every $t\geq n+c$, the image of $H^q(P^\bullet/I^tP^\bullet)\to H^q(P^\bullet/I^nP^\bullet)$ equals the fixed subgroup given by the image of $Z^q$ in the latter cohomology group. This proves algebraic image stabilization explicitly; no spectral-sequence or pro-category inference is needed.

source.place: Tag 00IN, lemma-Artin-Rees; direct cycle calculation replacing the Tor spectral-sequence last paragraph of proetale.tex Tag 09C5

proof.text: Let $T_n=\underline{P^\bullet/I^nP^\bullet}$ with their canonical quotient maps. Evaluation at the final object $W$ is exact by the weakly-contractible evaluation lemma. Therefore evaluation preserves quasi-isomorphisms, since exact functors preserve the kernels and images defining cohomology. Its termwise functor already factors through the derived localization and is its own right derived functor, so $H^q(R\Gamma(W,C))=H^q(C(W))$. By exactness of constant realization and evaluation, $H^q(W,T_n)=\underline{H^q(P^\bullet/I^nP^\bullet)}(W)$ naturally in $n$. The functor $V\mapsto\underline V(W)$ on $B$-modules is exact by the constant-module section lemma, so it preserves images (image is kernel of cokernel). Apply it to the two equal images in step 5. For $m=n+c$, and every $t\geq m$, the images of $H^q(W,T_t)\to H^q(W,T_n)$ and $H^q(W,T_m)\to H^q(W,T_n)$ agree.

source.place: Tag 09C5, exact-sections passage; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0946 and sites-modules.tex Tag 093J

proof.text: Keep $q,n$ and $m=n+c$ from step 6. For each $t\geq m$, choose any of the individual isomorphisms $T_t\simeq H_t$ obtained in step 4, as an isomorphism over $A_t=B/I^t$. Reduce this single isomorphism successively to levels $m$ and $n$. Tensor associativity identifies the reductions of $T_t$ with $T_m,T_n$ and those of $H_t$ with $H_m,H_n$. Naturality of the quotient units gives an isomorphism of the two composable-arrow diagrams $T_t\to T_m\to T_n$ and $H_t\to H_m\to H_n$: on a K-flat representative the unit is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and successive reductions send $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes ab$, so the direct and successive quotient arrows coincide. This includes repeated indices when $t=m$ or $m=n$. On hypercohomology the same isomorphism at level $n$ therefore identifies both transition images with those in step 6, proving their equality. The isomorphisms may vary with $t$; the equality of two subgroups is transported using a single level-$n$ isomorphism for each comparison, so a compatible infinite family was never required. This proves the stated Mittag–Leffler condition for every $q$.
